title: Skolemization: adding symbols for witnesses

based_on.title: Compactness and Completeness of Propositional Logic and First-Order Logic

summary: Replace existential choices by fresh function symbols, preserving models through suitable expansions and reducts.
abstract: Saying that every object has a companion does not name a companion for each object. We can add a function symbol to do that job, interpreting it by a choice of witnesses. This replaces an existential quantifier by a term, but the arguments of the new function matter: a witness may depend on choices made earlier, never on choices still to come. We carry out this construction for a sentence whose quantifiers have been moved to the front. Every model of the original sentence can be expanded to satisfy the resulting universal sentence, and every model of that universal sentence gives a model of the original by forgetting the added functions. Thus the construction preserves whether a model exists, although an arbitrary interpretation of the new symbols need not work.
